items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has been PRODUCED before the Special Executive Magistrate court at Mandir Marg police station, after his Friday preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 ahead of the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place. LiveLaw's live-update log records the production at 3:29 PM IST with 'heavy security outside Mandir Marg police station'; The Daily Jagran (original byline, updated 3:15 PM IST) confirms he was brought before the SEM court. The SEM's ruling — whether he is bound down, released, or held — is not yet reported. Ratna Singh, CJP's legal head, had demanded his release, calling the arrest unlawful since he 'merely urged people to unfurl the Tiranga'.
items.title: Dipke PRODUCED before SEM court at Mandir Marg (~3:29 PM IST); ruling still awaited

items.source_name: Multiple independent IG on-ground video reports (@strikeoriginals, @ayankh0107)
items.summary: The 2 PM Press Club of India → Jantar Mantar march split into parallel outcomes. One contingent (students, journalists, activists) marched toward Jantar Mantar and staged a 'flash protest' ~200 metres from the barricaded site with 'RECLAIM JANTAR MANTAR' and 'GYANESH MUST RESIGN' placards (field report by @strikeoriginals). A separate 'Justice Morcha' march from near the NSUI office walked about 100 metres before police intercepted it — buses were stopped and people detained, with detentions continuing (@ayankh0107 field report). Other ground clips show the march column moving toward the Vijay Chowk/Sansad Bhawan road before hitting police barricades. No violence reported.
items.title: 2 PM Press Club march: flash protest reaches Jantar Mantar approach; 'Justice Morcha' faction intercepted, detentions ongoing

items.event_time_ist: Thursday evening, Oct 15 (NYC); Friday morning IST, Oct 16
items.summary: CATCH-UP (event before this run, never logged in the feed): Booker Prize-winning author Salman Rushdie publicly backed the CJP at a fundraising dinner for the Asian American Writers Workshop in New York on Thursday night, calling the youth agitation 'the most hopeful moment for a very long time' and urging the audience to 'celebrate the cockroach' — 'India is boiling,' he said. Filmmaker Mira Nair, whose birthday was celebrated at the dinner, declared herself a 'cockroach mom' and said she was proud of those in India 'fighting for democracy'. First reported by writer Amitava Kumar on his Substack from the event, and carried by LiveMint and IPA Newspack.
items.title: Salman Rushdie ('celebrate the cockroach') and Mira Nair ('cockroach mom') endorse CJP at NYC fundraiser
